transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m having a hard time staying with things mentally. Like at work, I’ll start a safety briefing or go over a plan really trying to pay attention, and a few minutes in my mind’s already on three other job problems. Then I miss stuff I should’ve caught.
Have you always had trouble maintaining focus like this since you were a kid, or is this a new problem that started more recently?

No, it’s not new. I mean… it goes back pretty far. In elementary school, teachers were already telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat, talked out of turn, lost homework, that kind of thing. I’d rush through directions before I really understood what I was supposed to do.
Do you snore loudly or has anyone told you that you stop breathing or gasp during sleep, and do you feel excessively sleepy during the day despite getting enough hours of sleep?
I don’t think so. Nobody’s told me I stop breathing or anything like that. I mean, I’m tired sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m falling asleep all day if I got enough sleep.
Can you tell me about your current alcohol or drug use—how much and how often do you drink or use any substances?
I don’t really have much to say there. I might have a drink here and there, but… nothing regular. I don’t use drugs.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless, or noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Not really… I mean, I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or stopped enjoying things.

When your mind drifts to those other job problems, does it feel like you're worrying about them—like you can't stop thinking about what might go wrong—or is it more that your attention just wanders without any specific worry attached?

It’s more like my attention just wanders. I’ll be trying to listen in a safety briefing or going over a plan, and a few minutes later I’m thinking about three other job issues. Not really panicking about them… I just miss stuff I should’ve caught.
Do you notice this same kind of distractibility and forgetfulness affecting other areas of your life, like at home, in relationships, or when driving or managing personal tasks?

Yeah… it does. At home especially. My wife’s pretty tired of reminding me about stuff I said I’d take care of.

And at work it’s become… more of a problem. Missed follow-ups, not keeping the site coordination organized enough. My employer’s brought it up formally, so… it’s not just little things anymore.
